suggestions.title: Close reconcile can close a split parent whose children are still running; the last child's done then throws closed->done
suggestions.evidence: noDeliveredPr() only looks at the parent's own builds. After a split, PRs are delivered by child todos (sourceKind 'orchestration'), so a split parent in building or confirm passes both the sweep filter and the re-read just before the write, and transitionTodos(..., 'closed') runs on it. Later, setTodoPhase(child, 'done') calls settleSplitOnDone (todos.ts:554), which calls setTodoPhase(deps, parent.id, 'done') at todos.ts:601. assertPhaseTransition('closed', 'done') then throws PhaseTransitionError, after the child's own phase has already been written.
suggestions.failurePath: 1. The poller imports issue #N and the chief splits the task: the parent goes to confirm, then building, and the children run. 2. A triage-or-above user closes #N on GitHub, either directly or through a merged child PR that says 'closes #N'. 3. The next sweep closes the parent. Its children are not reconciled, so they keep running. 4. When the last child reaches done, the child's done path (builds.ts:216 or transitionTodos) throws out of settleSplitOnDone, and the parent stays closed instead of done. This throw already exists for a split parent closed by hand. The poller adds an automatic way to reach it. Possible fixes: skip todos that have children not yet done, or make settleSplitOnDone ignore a parent that is closed.

suggestions.title: Duplicate projects whose githubRepo differs only in case still give two tasks for one issue
suggestions.evidence: The poller picks the lowest-id project for a repo, compared case-insensitively (issue-intake.ts:825), and its own claimedRefs check ignores case. The webhook instead matches project.githubRepo exactly against payload.repository.full_name (webhook.ts:145). importGithubIssue's claimedSourceRefs (inArray, exact match) and the importsInFlight key (`${teamId}\u0000${ref}`) are both case-sensitive.
suggestions.failurePath: A team has project P1 'Acme/App' (lower id) and project P2 'acme/app', and GitHub's full_name is 'acme/app'. The poller imports #5 through P1 as github:Acme/App#5. Later, a 'pacman' label webhook maps to P2 and imports github:acme/app#5. The case-sensitive D4 check misses the existing task, and a second task is created. It also happens when the two imports run at the same time, because the claim keys differ. This needs a misconfigured pair of projects and the same exact-match check existed before this PR, but it qualifies the PR's 'one task' claim. Compare refs case-insensitively in claimedSourceRefs and in the claim key.

suggestions.title: Rate-limit failure mode: a rate-limited events or permission read does not stop the sweep, and no test covers more than one candidate under a limit
suggestions.evidence: take() turns a null events or permission read into 'not-taken' (issue-intake.ts:539-548), and the candidate loop moves on to the next unclaimed issue (issue-intake.ts:646-661). Only 'imported' or 'full' stops the loop, so while GitHub answers 403 x-ratelimit-remaining:0 or 429, every unclaimed labeled candidate (up to 300 per project over 3 pages) gets its own failing events read every sweep, and other projects and teams keep reading. Group 2 (issue-intake.test.ts:671-731) tests the 429 and 403-rate-limit responses with a single candidate only.
suggestions.failurePath: A project has 20 unclaimed ready-for-agent issues and room under the cap, and the token is rate-limited. Each 5-minute sweep sends 1 list read and 20 events reads, all of them rejected, for as long as the limit lasts. The ticket's failure mode '轮询打满 GitHub 速率' is handled only by conditional reads. A test with several candidates and a 403-ratelimit or 429 answer would show the extra reads; stopping the team's sweep on such an answer would remove them.

Tests issue-intake.test.ts:1114-1124 ('首见即 closed → 永不被对账关闭'), 1197-1210 ('重启…首见即 closed → 不关') and 1141-1155 (outside or deleted closer → not closed) assert that the task stays open. suggestions.failurePath: The server restarts (for example a P7 self-deploy) while a poller task's issue is closed by a maintainer. After the restart the first state read is 'closed', the issue is not in seenOpen, and the task stays in building or todo indefinitely; the tests pin that outcome. The same holds for an issue closed by a bot account without triage. This is deliberate and disclosed, but it changes a ticket failure mode, so the user merge should accept it explicitly.

suggestions.title: D5 cannot tell an agent's label from the owner's: labels applied through the Claude app count as the owner
suggestions.failurePath: When PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE is on, a Claude Code or in-product agent holding the owner's GitHub authorization can open an issue and apply ready-for-agent. The labeled event's actor is the owner and performed_via_github_app is 'claude'. newestLabeler returns that owner (line 282) and hasTriage passes. viaApp is only logged (lines 576-588), so the poller imports and orchestrates the task with no human in the loop. Agents can therefore feed themselves work, up to the cap of 3 per project.
suggestions.evidence: The captured fixture apps/server/test/fixtures/issue-intake/events-1406.json shows the ready-for-agent label on #1406 itself applied by actor xiechimon via app 'claude'. issue-intake.test.ts:2008 pins viaApp 'claude' as taken. The PR's Risk section accepts that an app acting on a user's behalf counts as that user. A possible fix: refuse a labeled event whose viaApp is set, or allow only a configured list of apps, until a human-only label path exists.

suggestions.title: Issue body and title are read at import time, not when labeled; an outside author can edit them after a maintainer labels
suggestions.failurePath: An outside user opens an issue and a triage-level maintainer applies ready-for-agent. The author can still edit the title and body, and does so before the next 5-minute sweep. labelerVerdict checks only who labeled. take() then calls importGithubIssue (line 556), which reads the current body (github-issues.ts:239) into todo.spec (line 254). orchestrateTodo then dispatches it automatically. The edited text reaches the chief's user message and, from there, workers with shell access on the daemon machine, with no human click. Before this PR, manual import was the main entry, and the webhook's pacman-label trigger was unchanged (#1459).
suggestions.evidence: D5 (ADR 0021) requires only the labeler check and body-as-data, and the body does stay out of the system layer (prompts.ts:288-307 quotes it in the user message). So this is within the ADR's letter, and the PR's Risk section acknowledges it. Possible mitigations: require the issue author to have triage or above as well, or keep a human start for issues by outside authors until the text can be bound to the moment of labeling.
